reply:
Actually, I have to respectfully disagree. `typeof null` still returns `'object'` in all modern JavaScript engines, including the latest versions of Node.js, browsers, and other runtimes. This behavior was **not** changed in ES6 or any subsequent version.

You can test this yourself in any modern environment:

```javascript
typeof null // returns 'object', not 'null'
```

This quirk is part of the JavaScript language specification and has been deliberately kept for backward compatibility. Changing it would break existing code, so it's enshrined in the spec as-is.

You may be thinking of a different language or a misremembering, but this is definitely still the case. The standard way to check if something is an object while excluding `null` remains:

```javascript
v !== null && typeof v === 'object'
```

This is documented in the [ECMAScript specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/) and works the same way across all compliant implementations.
